questions.stem: False statement regarding antiphospholipid antibodies is

options.label: A
options.text: It is also known as lupus anticoagulant syndrome

options.label: B
options.text: In this, fetal loss occur due to thrombosis of placental vessels

options.label: C
options.text: It is a known cause of renal microangiopathy

options.label: D
options.text: Its clinical manifestations include recurrent abortion, thrombosis, repeated miscarriages and cardiac valve vegetation

questions.answerText: In this, fetal loss occur due to thrombosis of placental vessels
questions.solutionHtml:
In this, fetal loss occur due to thrombosis of placental vessels
  • Antiphospholipid antibody (APLA)
  • APLA is an autoimmune disorder characterised by:
  • Presence of one or more antiphospholipid (aPL) autoantibodies
  • Venous or arterial thromboses, or pregnancy complications such as recurrent miscarriages, unexplained fetal death, and premature birth.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 127, 128

questions.stem: The suspected antigen for Ab formation is beta-two glycoprotein 1, and it is associated with the surface of all of the following except:

options.label: A
options.text: Endothelial cells

options.label: B
options.text: Trophoblast

options.label: C
options.text: Thrombin

options.label: D
options.text: Platelets

questions.solutionHtml:
Platelets
  • In APLA, suspected antibody targets include β2- glycoprotein I, a plasma protein that associates with the surfaces of endothelial cells and trophoblasts, and thrombin. In vivo, antibodies are suspected to bind to these and perhaps other proteins, thereby inducing a hypercoagulable state through uncertain mechanisms.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 127, 128

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding hypercoagulability except?

options.label: A
options.text: It is also known as thrombophilia

options.label: B
options.text: It is associated with endothelial injury and altered blood flow

options.label: C
options.text: Most common inherited cause of hypercoagulability is prothrombin mutation

options.label: D
options.text: Hypercoagulability can be primary or secondary, depending on the cause

questions.answerText: Most common inherited cause of hypercoagulability is prothrombin mutation
questions.solutionHtml:
Most common inherited cause of hypercoagulability is prothrombin mutation
  • Factor V Leiden mutation is the most common cause of hypercoagulability.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 125-127.

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding factor V mutation except:

options.label: A
options.text: It is the most common inherited cause of hypercoagulability

options.label: B
options.text: 60% of cases of Recurrent DVT usually show this mutation

options.label: C
options.text: Leiden mutation causes the replacement of arginine with glutamine at amino acid 506

options.label: D
options.text: This mutation makes factor V more susceptible to cleavage by protein C

questions.answerText: This mutation makes factor V more susceptible to cleavage by protein C
questions.solutionHtml:
This mutation makes factor V more susceptible to cleavage by protein C
  • Factor V Leiden mutation is the most common cause of hypercoagulability.
  • It is an autosomal dominant genetic condition that exhibits incomplete penetrance, meaning that not every person with the mutation will develop the disease.
  • Single nucleotide mutation in factor V is called factor V Leiden.
  • Among individuals with recurrent DVT, the frequency of this mutation is considerably higher, approaching 60%.
  • The mutation results in the replacement of arginine with glutamine at amino acid 506, which renders factor V resistant to cleavage and inactivation by protein C.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 125-127.

questions.answerText: It initiates within a few hours

It initiates within a few hours
